narrative: Markets are currently navigating a volatile period defined by the US midterm elections, a reassessment of the AI investment cycle, and shifting Middle East geopolitics. While diplomatic efforts regarding Iran have recently cooled oil prices, the Nasdaq 100 has entered a technical correction as investors demand proof of AI monetization. The Federal Reserve remains hawkish, with Chair Warsh signaling a potential December hike, while the US Treasury's upcoming refunding announcement is expected to influence the yield curve. Traders are largely viewing the midterms as a 'clearing event' that could potentially pave the way for a year-end relief rally.

Nasdaq.why: The index entered a technical correction as hedge funds deleverage tech holdings and Howard Marks (Oaktree) warns the AI 'bubble of infallibility' has burst.

S&P 500.why: Mike Wilson (Morgan Stanley) forecasts a 9% dip around the midterms before a rally toward 8,000, though futures have recently stabilized.

Gold.why: Gold broke below the key $4,000 technical level and is showing an unusual correlation with falling tech stocks according to Anthony Stephens.

Oil.why: Brent and WTI fell over 3% on reports that President Trump seeks diplomacy with Iran over military strikes, despite Goldman Sachs raising its long-term forecast to $105.

priced_in: 71% probability of a Democratic sweep of both chambers according to Kalshi
A 25 bps rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia to 4.85%
A technical correction in the Nasdaq 100 following AI spending fatigue
A Bank of England rate hike on Thursday
debates: Whether the tech sell-off is a localized earnings reassessment (Paul Donovan, UBS) or a broader credit and bubble risk (Howard Marks, Oaktree)
If the US Treasury will pivot issuance toward shorter-dated paper to manage interest costs
Whether the US midterm outcome will trigger a 'buy the dip' rally regardless of which party wins (Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley)
